goals: check every visible navigation and menu link works
open sections and report any page that errors or overflows the window

runs.notes: The only arm that browsed several target pages. It clicked Research, Blogs, Projects, then three nav controls that changed nothing, raised one dead control (Experience), then followed a footer link to LinkedIn at step 11. Most of its 37 broken-link rows were measured on LinkedIn's own pages after that, so they describe LinkedIn, not the target.

All 25 executed clicks chose the same hero control, which stopped changing the page after the second. The dead control is real and corroborated; the repetition is a model-quality finding. The two broken links are bot walls (LinkedIn 999, Behance 400) and stayed candidates.

The page had real controls, and the model still answered BLOCKED against a login-gated guest view without clicking anything. The single candidate is two console errors on one row: an inline theme script and the Cloudflare insights beacon, both refused by the site's own script-src 'self' policy, independently confirmed from response headers.

Clicked Sign in, reached the credentials form, then chose TYPE_TEXT on the Email field. A loopback arm carries no text source, so the browser call failed with a CDP parameter error: the harness artifact, not a site defect, and it ended the walk. The other two candidates are the same CSP console errors the Jev row recorded.

dropped_arms.laya: Owner direction 2026-09-29: the Laya arm is excluded from this comparison. Its post-settle passes (2 steps on the target site, 1 stale recovery) are recorded on issue #9 and are not part of the matrix above.

known_gaps: TYPE_TEXT on loopback arms has no text source, so a form field produces a browser_error finding attributed to the target URL
the walk can leave the target origin and then measure third-party pages as if they belonged to the site
the layout detector flags decorative off-canvas elements and sub-pixel box-model differences
the stale recovery budget of three ends a walk on a permanently animating page with terminal stale_page
a login-gated page can produce an immediate BLOCKED with no interaction, which is a model decision, not a site result
